## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 124.0.0.125
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/virtual-appliance-release-notes-version-124-0-0-125/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:06:10+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:26:21.783492+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 124.0.0.125 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 124.0.0.125
Release Date: May 27, 2025
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 124.0.0.125
Upgrading to Version 124.0.0.125
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 117.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 117.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than or equal to 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
Important
Due to space limitations on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition, you must complete the following steps to upgrade to Appliance software version 124.0.0.125.
To upgrade to Appliance software version 124.0.0.125:
Log in to nsshell.
Use the following command to download the appliance software AUP package:
upgrade download software version 124.0.0.125
You must delete all other packages. For DPoP, you must delete the urldb, threat-feed, and software packages. For OPLP, you must delete the threat-feed and software packages.
Use the following commands to see all listed versions of the packages:
upgrade urldb list
upgrade threat-feed list
upgrade software list
Use the following commands to delete all listed versions:
Note
Do not delete the 124.0.0.125 software package.
For all package types, you must delete the locally available packages. You cannot delete the remotely available packages.
upgrade urldb delete version $version
upgrade threat-feed delete version $version
upgrade software delete version $version
To prepare the software package, run the following commands:
upgrade software prepare version 124.0.0.125
upgrade software status prepare
If you are unable to prepare the software package, you must contact Netskope Support.
For DPoP, you must download the urldb package before installing Appliance version 124.0.0.125. Use the
upgrade urldb list
command, then download the latest version with the
upgrade urldb download $Version
command.
Use the following command to upgrade to Appliance version 124.0.0.125:
upgrade software install version 124.0.0.125
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Rolling Back Version 124.0.0.125
To roll back Appliance software version 124.0.0.125:
Log in to nsshell and use the following command:
rollback software-image
Note that the status for
mongodb
will be
FATAL
.
Exit nsshell and select bash using a one-time token.
Run the following commands:
lcgo lcmongo-infrastructure
nsadmin@lcmongo-infrastructure:~$ sudo rm -rf /var/lib/mongodb/*
nsadmin@lcmongo-infrastructure:~$ sudo supervisorctl restart mongodb
mongodb: ERROR (not running)
mongodb: started
Log in to nsshell again. All services should be
RUNNING
except for
mongoinit
.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 113.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 124.0.0.125 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 117.0.0, 121.0.0, and 124.0.0.125, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 117.0.0
117.0.0
117.0.0
124.0.0.125
121.0.0
124.0.0.125
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.

## Netskope Device Intelligence Release Notes in Version 25.04
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-device-intelligence-release-notes-in-version-25-04/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:04:28+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:26:24.007111+00:00

Netskope Device Intelligence Release Notes in Version 25.04 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Device Intelligence Release Notes in Version 25.04
We are excited to announce our recent updates on the product! Get the features, issues fixed, and other updates published in the month of April, i.e. in 25.04 version release notes.
Release Notes Subscription
Would you like to subscribe to our release notes? To learn more:
Release Notes Subscription
.
Here is the list of new features and enhancements released in 25.04 version.
u003cstrongu003eUser Account Creation and Managementu003c/strongu003e
The user account creation and management changes in Non-SSO and SSO flows.
Non-SSO Flow
Users can create accounts across multiple tenants, even if they already exist in another tenant. Each account is created per tenant, granting access regardless of existing accounts in other tenants.
SSO Flow
The “allow_domains” property in the wootcloud collection permits domain-based account creation across tenants. Users from specified domains can create multiple accounts, while those from unlisted domains cannot.
Device Intelligence Single UI Experience
With this release, you will see integrated Device Intelligence into the Netskope dashboard.
The integration aims to create a unified user interface, avoiding new page or tab openings.
Users should navigate to Device Intelligence within the same tab to maintain a seamless Netskope dashboard experience.
UI Enhancements in Manage
With this release, you can now directly click on the field to edit the values in
Manage
>
Assets
menu. Previously, a pencil icon was provided, which is removed now.

## Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for April 2025
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-digital-experience-management-release-notes-for-april-2025/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:03:17+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:26:35.094284+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for April 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for April 2025
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of April 2025:
This release provides several improvements to your DEM experience, focusing on improving the user experience and offering more flexible configuration options.
Enhanced Network Visualization
New Interactive Traceroute Map:
Gain a more intuitive understanding of network paths with the redesigned traceroute visualization. This new view includes:
Clear displays of your customer site and the Netskope network.
Provides richer node information.
Automatically keeps auto-diagnostic enabled when you turn it on.
Offers a better and more explicit focus view when investigating specific nodes.
Shows more detailed information like IP addresses as you zoom in (use “shift + mouse wheel” for easy zoom).
Includes a convenient map legend in the top right and settings in the top left for customization.
Improved Path Performance Dashboard:
The first six widgets on the Path Performance dashboard are now shorter, allowing you to see a portion of the new traceroute visualization without needing to scroll.
Smarter Legend Colors:
The map legend now utilizes an intelligent algorithm to ensure better differentiation between colors, even when multiple inputs have similar hues.
Improved User Interface Performance
Faster Loading:
The loading process has been optimized, resulting in a noticeably faster initial loading experience.
Flexible Enterprise Station Configuration
Downloadable Docker Compose File:
For customers managing their own virtual machines with Docker, you now have the option to download a standalone Docker Compose file. This option offers enhanced flexibility in the deployment process.

## Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for March 2025
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-digital-experience-management-release-notes-for-march-2025/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:03:18+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:26:36.200156+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for March 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for March 2025
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of March 2025:
Auto-Detection of Domains for Station’s Predefined Apps
The configuration process for Application Probes within a Station has been streamlined. Previously, manual selection of domains was required when establishing predefined applications. This functionality has been updated to align with NSClient behavior—domains are now automatically populated. Domains are derived from NSProxy, based on the most used domains per tenant. This eliminates ambiguity in configuration. Simply set the app, and Netskope will manage the domains.
Timeseries Legend Improvements
Enhancements have been made to the timeseries legend to provide improved readability and usability. These improvements offer increased clarity and a more streamlined layout for faster analysis.

---
## Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for February 2025
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-digital-experience-management-release-notes-for-february-2025/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:03:18+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:26:37.330234+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for February 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for February 2025
Dashboard Auto-refresh Improvement
In order to enhance the user experience and prevent the occurrence of unexpected reloads, a dynamic icon has been added. The purpose of this icon is to visually indicate the time remaining before the next reload.
An Alternative (BETA) Graph Visualization for Network Path
The visualization of routers, POPs, and latency within a graph has always been a key and popular feature of DEM! This release includes enhancements that improve the layout and clearly define the Netskope Area, tenant site, and other zones. More enhancements are on the way, but for now, early adopters are able to experience these updates by clicking “Switch to new view”.

## Netskope One DSPM 11.0 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-11-0-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:05:22+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:26:40.650046+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 11.0 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 11.0 Release Notes
Major New Features
DSPM for SaaS Applications
We’re excited to introduce DSPM for SaaS, expanding our Data Security Posture Management capabilities to Microsoft OneDrive, SharePoint Online, and Google Drive. This enhancement provides organizations with instant visibility into what data is stored, where it resides, and how it’s being accessed within these SaaS applications.
With these insights, security teams can:
Identify and protect sensitive data stored in different user drives or shared sites;
Define and enforce security policies based on proactive risk assessments; and
Conduct deeper scans on high-risk areas to prevent potential exposure.
To further simplify data security management, we offer unified visibility offering key insights across IaaS, PaaS, on-premises environments, and now SaaS—providing a unified view of sensitive data, access controls, and security posture.
This expanded coverage empowers security teams to proactively safeguard data, strengthen compliance, and reduce risk across their entire cloud ecosystem.
DSPM Availability Within The Netskope Console
Netskope One DSPM, previously accessible only via a separate login, can now be accessed & managed from directly within the Netskope console. With this new seamless navigation experience, the value of the Netskope One platform increases thanks to the synergy provided by DSPM being available alongside your other products such as Next-Gen API Data Protection, SaaS Security Posture Management, Data Loss Prevention, and more!
Security teams can efficiently perform analysis & investigation of their combined IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS security posture, without the pain of jumping back-and-forth between separate interfaces
Administrators can now manage a single set of users, RBAC roles, and API keys, instead of double-keying everything
API keys are now enhanced, with scope limitations and expiration dates
Existing customers will require an upgrade to access this new experience. Your account team will reach out to further discuss the changes and schedule your migration soon.

Netskope Cloud Exchange Release Notes Version 5.1.2 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Cloud Exchange Release Notes Version 5.1.2
Release Date: July 7, 2025
New Features and Enhancements
Added
Core
UI
Support for more granular maintenance window selection for Risk Exchange Actions.
Added support for pulling logs from 3rd-party platforms in the Log Shipper module.
Support for more granular maintenance window selection for Risk Exchange Actions, including the ability to specify days of the week.
Changed
Core
UI
Updated python version to 3.11.
Updated python libraries.
Updated MongoDB version to 8.0.6.
Updated RabbitMQ version to 4.1.0.
Enhanced plugin configuration disable and delete workflow.
Cloud Exchange as a VM (OVA and Hyper-V) users will be asked for
cteadmin
password each time the command is run with the
sudo
prefix.
Log Shipper and Ticket Orchestrator plugin execution workflow to support storing of additional data in the plugin configuration.
CSP headers for more secure access of UI.
Removed
Core
UI
NA
NA
Fixed Issues
Core
UI
Fixed the workflow when the required approval is disabled for Risk Exchange Actions.
Fixed an issue for the Ticket Orchestrator Queue configuration to support all the fields for direct mapping.
Fixed the Filtering capability on complex fields through Business rules (like list and nested objects).
Fixed Risk Exchange default schema indexes.
Fixed setup script to avoid redundant sudo prefix.
Fixed the Threat Exchange Sharing configuration update workflow to limit the use of same Netskope targets (like File Hash list and URL list).
Fixed a filtering issue for the
dlp_incident_id
,
connection_id
,
app_session_id
,
dlp_parent_id
, and
browser_session_id
fields in Business rules.
Fixed the length limitation for the maintenance password.
Fixed the Ticket Orchestrator page rendering issue when an alert or event is expanded.
Fixed the Risk Exchange Actions update workflow to adapt changes of the plugin Action labels and parameters.
Known Issues and Limitations For 5.1.2
Earlier versions of the Netskope ITSM (Ticket Orchestrator) plugin did not support filtering on fields with complex data types, such as lists of strings, dictionaries, or lists of dictionaries in alerts/events. In order to fix this issue, upgrade to the Ticket Orchestrator plugin version 2.2.0 (or the latest version available), included with the Cloud Exchange v5.1.2 onwards.
In case of an action label change for Risk Exchange plugins, user may see the previous label for the configured actions until the actions updated again.
Business rule filtering for the fields value having
is not supported.
When the static Risk Exchange action parameters value starts with
$
, it will be treated as Source type of action parameter only.
Intermittently few of the celery tasks may gets stuck and cause disk pile up. Restarting Cloud Exchange should resolve the issue.
If you migrate from 5.0.1 to 5.1.2, User Risk Exchange and Application Risk Exchange records will be listed in the Risk Exchange module, but they will not be qualified for the actions until the same records are pulled again from the source.

## Netskope One DSPM 11.1 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-11-1-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:05:22+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:27:16.235605+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 11.1 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 11.1 Release Notes
Major New Features
Support for Discovery & Classification of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Data Stores
Netskope One DSPM now offers the capability to scan Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) compartments, allowing for the discovery of child compartments and the data services within them. Connect Oracle Base Database Service, Oracle Autonomous Database Service and Oracle Exadata Database Service for discovery and classification. This expanded coverage for OCI significantly enhances visibility into sensitive data across different environments.
Support for Data Discovery & Classification for Box
Netskope One DSPM now supports classifying data within Box application. Expanded coverage for Box provides enhanced visibility into all sensitive data across your on-prem and cloud environments.
On-Prem IBM DB2
Netskope One DSPM now supports classifying data within On-prem IBM DB2 databases. Expanded coverage provides enhanced visibility into all sensitive data across your on-prem and cloud environments.

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 128.0.0
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/virtual-appliance-release-notes-version-128-0-0/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:06:00+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:27:17.672974+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 128.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 128.0.0
Release Date: August 5, 2025
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 128.0.0
Upgrading to version 128.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 121.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 121.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
Important
Due to space limitations on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition, when upgrading to Appliance software version 128.0.0 directly from version 121.0.0, you must complete the following steps.
To upgrade to Appliance software version 128.0.0 directly from version 121.0.0:
Log in to nsshell.
Use the following command to download the appliance software AUP package:
upgrade download software version 128.0.0.153
You must delete all other packages. For DPoP, you must delete the urldb, threat-feed, and software packages. For OPLP, you must delete the threat-feed and software packages.
Use the following commands to see all listed versions of the packages:
upgrade urldb list
upgrade threat-feed list
upgrade software list
Use the following commands to delete all listed versions:
Note
Do not delete the 128.0.0.153 software package.
For all package types, you must delete the locally available packages. You cannot delete the remotely available packages.
upgrade urldb delete version $version
upgrade threat-feed delete version $version
upgrade software delete version $version
To prepare the software package, run the following commands:
upgrade software prepare version 128.0.0.153
upgrade software status prepare
If you are unable to prepare the software package, you must contact Netskope Support.
For DPoP, you must download the urldb package before installing Appliance version 128.0.0.153. Use the
upgrade urldb list
command, then download the latest version with the
upgrade urldb download $Version
command.
Use the following command to upgrade to Appliance version 128.0.0.153:
upgrade software install version 128.0.0.153
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Rolling Back Version 128.0.0.153
To roll back Appliance software version 128.0.0.153:
Log in to nsshell and use the following command:
rollback software-image
Note that the status for
mongodb
will be
FATAL
.
Exit nsshell and select bash using a one-time token.
Run the following commands:
lcgo lcmongo-infrastructure
nsadmin@lcmongo-infrastructure:~$ sudo rm -rf /var/lib/mongodb/*
nsadmin@lcmongo-infrastructure:~$ sudo supervisorctl restart mongodb
mongodb: ERROR (not running)
mongodb: started
Log in to nsshell again. All services should be
RUNNING
except for
mongoinit
.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 110.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 128.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 121.0.0, 124.0.0.125, and 128.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 121.0.0
121.0.0
121.0.0
128.0.0
124.0.0.125
128.0.0
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.
Hash Values for Virtual Appliance Installation Files
The following table provides the md5sum and sha256sum values for the Virtual Appliance installer files on VMware ESX, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Linux KVM platforms for version 128.0.0.

## Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for August 2025
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-digital-experience-management-release-notes-for-august-2025/
**Last Modified:** 2025-11-03T19:36:12+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:27:32.123176+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for August 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for August 2025
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of August 2025:
Site Based Alerting
Three new alert types have been introduced to generate notifications for the following scenarios:
Site-to-POP Performance:
Notifications will be triggered when the aggregate latency measured between designated “Sites” and Netskope POPs exceeds a configured threshold for a specified duration.
Site-to-Application Performance:
Notifications will be generated based on the aggregate latency (time to first byte) measured from defined “Sites” to applications, should this measurement breach a configured threshold for a set duration.
Site-to-Application Availability:
Notifications will be issued when the aggregate availability percentage measured for defined “Sites” to applications falls below a configured threshold for a set duration.
Bulk Import/Export of Sites and Gateways
A new bulk import and export feature within the DEM settings UI facilitates the streamlined management of sites and gateway objects. This feature includes the following:
Large quantities of sites and/or gateways can be readily imported in CSV, JSON, or YAML formats.
Extensive numbers of sites and/or gateways can be effortlessly exported into CSV, JSON, or YAML formats.
Modifications to exported lists of sites and/or gateways can be undertaken, with subsequent reimportation confidently executed through the native “compare” feature, which enables verification of impending changes prior to overwriting.
Enhancements to Traceroute Visualization and Accuracy
The Traceroute feature has been improved with a variety of enhancements. This release includes the following enhancements:
Traceroute visuals have been updated for a clearer user experience.
Shift + Scroll
now zooms in/out on traceroute diagrams.
Traceroute paths and latency are now derived from backend APIs for improved accuracy.

## Netskope One DSPM 11.2 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-11-2-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2025-09-02T15:56:30+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:27:46.489000+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 11.2 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 11.2 Release Notes
Major New Features
DSPM for Salesforce (SFDC)
Netskope One DSPM now offers the capability to scan Salesforce (SFDC) content libraries, allowing for the classification of documents and the discovery of sensitive data. This expanded coverage for SFDC significantly enhances visibility into sensitive data in a critical business application. It’s important to note that only data classification will be performed, with risk assessment to be delivered in later phases. The Salesforce Classic version will not be supported, and we will only scan the “Owned by me library.”
Configuration & Privilege Analysis for On-Premises IBM Db2
Netskope One DSPM now offers the capability to perform Configuration Analysis and Deep Privilege Analysis for on-premises IBM Db2 data stores. This new functionality provides valuable insights into the security posture of your IBM Db2 instances, including misconfiguration risks and who has access to sensitive data. This expanded coverage significantly enhances visibility into data risks within on-premises environments.
Support for custom DLP Profiles and Rules in DSPM for SaaS Applications
DSPM for SaaS Applications now supports the ability to select custom DLP Profiles & Rules to scan against your SaaS applications. Now you can enable / disable any type of DLP Profile, regardless of type (pre-defined or custom). For your existing connections, you can update your selected profiles, and changes will take effect at the next scan.

**Last Modified:** 2025-11-03T19:48:31+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:27:55.445132+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for September 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for September 2025
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of September 2025:
DEM Browser Extension: Performance Monitoring & Intelligence
We’re excited to share significant enhancements to digital experience monitoring for Netskope. This release introduces real user monitoring, at the transaction level, capabilities for both steered and bypassed browser based applications, along with new workflows to help admins troubleshoot faster and with greater context. The enhanced intelligence that these new features unlock, provide admins with smarter insights and access to user specific drilldowns with high-accuracy actionable data.
What’s new:
Performance telemetry collection from end users’ browsers
Apps dependencies automated discovery (CDN providers, 3rd-party infra, etc.)
Page load and API calls performance telemetry
Local connectivity and network path impact
App server performance
Data transfer and transactional error
Steered and bypassed browser based application monitoring
Monitoring of browser based application performance for both steered and bypassed applications is natively supported. Simply configure your application URL patterns and apply the policy.
Netskope client is
NOT
required
Monitoring holistic user experience based on device, network, and application metrics is now possible for users where the Netskope client is not deployed or used as a steering mechanism.
For the complete list of capabilities, refer to
Browser Extension Metrics
.
To learn how to configure Private Application Monitoring, refer to
Browser Extension
.
DEM NPA: Performance Monitoring & Intelligence
We’re excited to share significant enhancements to private app experience monitoring in DEM. This release introduces real user monitoring capabilities for private apps, along with new workflows to help admins troubleshoot faster and with greater context. The enhanced intelligence that these new features unlock, provide admins with smarter insights and access to user specific drilldowns with high-accuracy actionable data.
What’s new:
Network Path Visualization
A new visualization maps all paths between users and private applications, helping admins quickly identify routing gaps, publisher issues, and performance bottlenecks across each path segment between user and the private application.
Root Cause Analysis with NPA Metrics
NPA performance monitoring is now integrated into root cause analysis, enabling identification of degradations caused by both network and application issues.
“Other Impacted Users” Metric
A new metric highlights users experiencing similar degradations across the network, making it easier to detect systemic issues and pinpoint shared infrastructure problems.
For the complete list of capabilities, refer to
Private Application Metrics.
To learn how to configure Private Application Monitoring, refer to
Monitored Applications
.
Tunnel Status Alert Notifications
We’ve enhanced the Tunnel Status Alert feature to provide a consistent and detailed experience across all notification types.
Now, when you use a custom webhook for Tunnel Status Alerts, the notification payload will include the same detailed information that was previously available only in Slack and email notifications. This change ensures that incident notifications for tunnel status are standardized, allowing for richer, more consistent data to be delivered to your external systems.
Terminology Changes
What’s new:
Terminology changes have been made to the DEM “Tenant Overview” dashboard, specifically the “POP & Service Status“ widget, to more accurately represent the activities occurring across the Netskope data centers and services.
Terminology changes have been made to the DEM Alerts “Platform > Service Status“ alert type. The triggered alerts will showcase the new terminology, as well as the email and webhook notification templates. This new terminology will more accurately represent the activities occurring across the Netskope data centers and services.

## Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for October 2025
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-digital-experience-management-release-notes-for-october-2025/
**Last Modified:** 2025-11-14T18:01:47+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:28:29.362374+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for October 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for October 2025
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of October 2025:
Enhanced IPSEC/GRE Tunnel Error Reporting for DEM
We’ve added a new column “Error” to the “Tunnel Status” widget of the “Network Steering” section of DEM. This column will contain the technical error reason for why the IPSEC/GRE tunnel is in a down state. Additionally, DEM tunnel status and tunnel flapping alerts have also been enhanced to include the “Error” in both the tunnel alert details screen and the notification email templates and webhook payloads.
DEM Browser Extension: Performance Monitoring & Intelligence
We’re excited to share significant enhancements to digital experience monitoring for Netskope. This release introduces real user monitoring, at the transaction level, capabilities for both steered and bypassed browser based applications, along with new workflows to help admins troubleshoot faster and with greater context. The enhanced intelligence that these new features unlock, provide admins with smarter insights and access to user specific drilldowns with high-accuracy actionable data.
What’s new:
Performance telemetry collection from end users’ browsers
Apps dependencies automated discovery (CDN providers, 3rd-party infra, etc.)
Page load and API calls performance telemetry
Local connectivity and network path impact
App server performance
Data transfer and transactional error
Steered and bypassed browser based application monitoring
Monitoring of browser based application performance for both steered and bypassed applications is natively supported. Simply configure your application URL patterns and apply the policy.
Netskope client is
NOT
required
Monitoring holistic user experience based on device, network, and application metrics is now possible for users where the Netskope client is not deployed or used as a steering mechanism.
For the complete list of capabilities, refer to
Browser Extension Metrics
To learn how to configure Private Application Monitoring, refer to
Browser Extension

A new visualization maps all paths between users and private applications, helping admins quickly identify routing gaps, publisher issues, and performance bottlenecks across each path segment between user and the private application.
Root Cause Analysis with NPA Metrics
NPA performance monitoring is now integrated into root cause analysis, enabling identification of degradations caused by both network and application issues.
“Other Impacted Users” Metric
A new metric highlights users experiencing similar degradations across the network, making it easier to detect systemic issues and pinpoint shared infrastructure problems.
For the complete list of capabilities, refer to
Private Application Metrics.
To learn how to configure Private Application Monitoring, refer to
Monitored Applications
.
Tunnel Status Alert Notifications
We’ve enhanced the Tunnel Status Alert feature to provide a consistent and detailed experience across all notification types.
Now, when you use a custom webhook for Tunnel Status Alerts, the notification payload will include the same detailed information that was previously available only in Slack and email notifications. This change ensures that incident notifications for tunnel status are standardized, allowing for richer, more consistent data to be delivered to your external systems.
Terminology Changes
Terminology changes have been made to the DEM “Tenant Overview” dashboard, specifically the “POP & Service Status“ widget, to more accurately represent the activities occurring across the Netskope data centers and services.
Terminology changes have been made to the DEM Alerts “Platform > Service Status“ alert type. The triggered alerts will showcase the new terminology, as well as the email and webhook notification templates. This new terminology will more accurately represent the activities occurring across the Netskope data centers and services.

## Netskope One DSPM 11.3 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-11-3-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2026-03-03T16:57:57+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:28:47.176705+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 11.3 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 11.3 Release Notes
Major New Features
New On-Prem Deployment Option for DSPM Sidecars
To benefit customers who prefer the ability to manage sidecars as virtual machines instead of containers, DSPM sidecars are now packaged in the Open Virtualization Archive (OVA) format for deployment in compatible VMWare VSphere hypervisors.
Improvements and Updates
AWS Infrastructure Onboarding Improvements
To reduce friction when onboarding infrastructure, the following changes have been made starting with the Add AWS Infrastructure Connection flow (both for adding accounts and organizations)
The following changes were made to the CloudFormation template and Terraform scripts:
The CloudFormation template and Terraform scripts have been reorganized to better-group permissions by the in-application capability they control. This way, if you wish to not provide the DSPM application with permission to any specific capability, it is easy to select & remove the relevant permissions without affecting the others
In addition, the CloudFormation template and Terraform scripts have been documented inline to explain each permission grouping, so it is clear why Netskope is requesting the permissions
Our
online documentation
has been updated to reflect the same reorganization and documentation of permissions. So if you choose not to grant Netskope access for a capability today but change your mind in the future, we now provide clear, easy instructions on how to add back the missing permissions to your CloudFormation or Terraform stacks
Within the application itself, changes were made to the Add Infrastructure Connection UI:
Cleared explanations are now available on the Capabilities tab, so you understand which each toggle does. Where supporting documentation is available, links are now shown to relevant articles on
docs.netskope.com
.
When you finalize & submit your Infrastructure Connection request, the UI will check your service account’s health and provide feedback if any expected permissions are missing
SMB Connection Improvements
Previously, only IPv4 addresses were acceptable as endpoint values for SMB connections. Now you DSPM will accept public hostnames for the endpoint (for example,
example.us-west-2.compute.amazonaws.com
).
In addition, special character support has been added for SMB file share / mount names. The following valid characters can now be used:
! @ # $ % & ' _ - . ~ ( ) { }

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 132.0.1
Release Date: February 4, 2026
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 132.0.1
Upgrading to version 132.0.1
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 124.0.0.125. If you are running appliance versions older than 124.0.0.125, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
450 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 110.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 132.0.1 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 124.0.0.125, 128.0.0, and 132.0.1, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 124.0.0.125
124.0.0.125
124.0.0.125
132.0.1
128.0.0
132.0.1
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.

**Last Modified:** 2026-01-27T04:37:24+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:29:30.834273+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for December 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for December 2025
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of December 2025:
DEM Licensing
A DEM licensing page has been released to aid customers in managing and maintaining their utilization of DEM-related features. This page contains the number of users activated for DEM monitoring, applications monitored, and enterprise stations active.
Disk Score
The Disk Score, which is a part of the Device Score, has been updated. This change will lower the score of devices which match the following criteria:
Having a disk of more than 500,000 KB
Having less than 10% of disk availability

**Last Modified:** 2026-03-31T15:05:03+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:29:44.213299+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for February 2026 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for February 2026
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of February 2026:
Google Chat Alert Notifications
DEM Alerting now supports Google Chat as a Webhook receiver for Alert notifications.
Learn more
.
User Overview Map Accuracy Fix
Fixed an issue where user counts on the
User Overview
map were displayed incorrectly. User counts on the map now accurately reflect actual usage data.
Historical View Fixes for User Overview and Device Details
Corrected a UI issue where timeframe parameters were not passed correctly, causing Historical views in
User Overview
and
Device Details
to show current data. Historical data views now show the selected time range.
DEM Configuration Workflow Improvements
Migrated resource configuration workflows from standalone pages to
contextual side panels
.
The
Create
workflow is now initiated from the primary list view.
The
Edit
workflow is now integrated into the resource detail view.
Previous behavior: These actions formerly redirected users to separate pages.

## Netskope One DSPM 12.0 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-12-0-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2026-03-03T16:42:29+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:30:03.054207+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 12.0 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 12.0 Release Notes
Major New Features
DSPM integration with DLP
DSPM has switched to fully utilize DLP as its classification engine, leading to several customer benefits:
All Netskope data inspection and classification is now performed using the same industry-leading DLP solution, whether it’s inline, data-at-rest, endpoint, etc.
DLP functionality is extended to previously-inaccessible areas, allowing customers to protect data-at-rest and classify structured data stores thru the addition of the new Column Classification rule type.
Instead of maintaining a separate list of Sensitive Data Type identifiers, customers can now reuse existing DLP Profile & Rule definitions to scan & classify data within DSPM
DLP dramatically expands the number of file types supported for inspection, from three dozen to over 2000, and data types from 5 dozen to nearly 4000
Exposure and Access Analysis for SaaS Data Stores
Netskope One DSPM now offers Sensitive Data Exposure and Access Analysis for SaaS applications. This new capability provides deep visibility into the security posture of your SaaS data stores, identifying over-shared sensitive files and tracking external user access, including those from personal email domains. To help administrators prioritize efforts, DSPM computes granular risk ratings for each data store, factoring in data exposure and external access risks. The enhanced User Assessment view consolidates a user’s access to sensitive files across all SaaS apps into a single pane, significantly improving the ability to manage data sharing practices and reduce the risk of data breaches.
Support for NetApp ONTAP
Netskope One DSPM now supports classifying data within NetApp ONTAP databases. This includes both AWS FSx for NetApp ONTAP and on-prem NetApp ONTAP. Expanded coverage provides enhanced visibility into all sensitive data across your on-prem and cloud environments.
Improvements and Updates
Deprecation of Azure MariaDB
Microsoft
deprecated support for Azure Database for MariaDB last September
. As a result, support for creating its data store connections has been removed from DSPM.
Proxy Support Added for DSPM Sidecar
DSPM sidecars can now be configured for explicit HTTPS proxy connections. New sidecars can be configured using an optional deployment parameter, while existing sidecars will require an upgrade to take advantage of this new functionality. For details on how to setup proxy, visit the
Deploying DSPM Sidecars category
and access the article specific to your sidecar deployment method.
Revamped File Details Drawer
The Classification Management Files tab has been revamped to make it easier to manage multiple files at once. Files are now presented in a compact list, allowing for more files to be presented on the screen at once. The most-important information is immediately-displayed, while richer detail such as rule & entity data type matches, file size, and more is available in a new slide-out drawer.
Onboarding Enhancements for GCP and Azure
As was previously-done for AWS, within the application itself, changes were made to the Add Infrastructure Connection UI for GCP and Azure:
Clear explanations are now available on the Capabilities tab, so you understand what each toggle does. Where supporting documentation is available, links are now shown to relevant articles on
docs.netskope.com
.
When you finalize & submit your Infrastructure Connection request, the UI will check your service account’s health and provide feedback if any expected permissions are missing
Support for connecting multiple mount points per SMB endpoint
When configuring a SMB data store connection, DSPM now supports creating multiple connections for the same endpoint using different mount points. For example, you could create one data store connection for the endpoint
1.2.3.4
and mount
share
, then another for endpoint
1.2.3.4
and mount
backup
.

## Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for March 2026
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-digital-experience-management-release-notes-for-march-2026/
**Last Modified:** 2026-03-31T14:57:46+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:30:19.010836+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for March 2026 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for March 2026
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of March 2026:
DEM Data Intelligence Agent: Generative AI for DEM
We’re excited to share
significant enhancements
to Netskope One Digital Experience Management. This release introduces the DEM Data Intelligence Agent, which integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with DEM data to transform granular telemetry and raw metrics into actionable insights accessed via natural language in an easy to use conversational interface. These capabilities help admins troubleshoot faster and allow for deeper contextuality in follow-ups. The enhanced intelligence that these new features unlock provides admins with
smarter insights
and
reduces time-to-task
by summarizing complex data into high-accuracy actionable insights.
What’s new:
Conversational Data Discovery:
Enable faster troubleshooting by allowing admins to ask direct questions in natural language to uncover insights like underperforming ISPs, degraded user experiences, and latency issues.
Assisted Root Cause Analysis:
Analyze network data in real-time to detect anomalies and automatically identify the root causes of network and performance problems.
Maintenance Forecasting:
Learn patterns to predict future network demands, node failures, and throughput needs, enabling proactive maintenance and efficient resource allocation.
Executive Summary
: Generate concise, high-level summaries of complex performance data for executive stakeholders, highlighting critical trends and key issues without requiring manual data interpretation.
DEM Insights
The new
Insights
page provides a unified, 360-degree view of the digital health of your entire organization. It allows administrators to monitor the performance of users, sites, applications, and infrastructure from a single, centralized dashboard. By leveraging performance telemetry from the Netskope Client, the Insights page helps you quickly determine if a performance impairment is localized to a user’s device, their Wi-Fi signal, a specific ISP, or the application itself.
Key capabilities of the Insights page include:
Global Insights Map
: A geographic visualization of your environment that can be toggled between
Users
and
Sites
. The map uses color-coded indicators to represent health status, allowing you to isolate regional performance dips at a glance.
Comprehensive Filtering
: Refine your view using the Filter Menu to drill down by:
Time
: View data ranges from the last hour to several days.
User Group/OU
: Identify if performance issues are systemic to specific departments or organizational units.
Applications
: Isolate performance metrics for specific monitored SaaS or Private apps.
Site
: Focus on specific office locations or branch environments.
Targeted Performance Metrics
: The dashboard includes dedicated widgets to pinpoint common bottlenecks:
Devices with Performance Issues
: Tracks hardware health by monitoring CPU and memory overutilization.
Wi-Fi Networks with Poor Signal
: Identifies users struggling with weak or unstable wireless connections.
ISPs with Highest Latencies
: Ranks Internet Service Providers based on round-trip time (RTT) to help differentiate between local connectivity issues and broader provider outages.
RBAC Support
: The Insights page is fully integrated with Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Ensure your administrator roles have the appropriate permissions enabled under
Settings > Administration > Roles
within the Digital Experience Management section.
DEM Alerts – Additional TTFB Options
Currently when configuring a site based application performance alert, users are limited to the TTFB times. We have added the following new options for selection: 2000ms, 2500ms, 3000ms, 3500ms, 4000ms to the TTFB times
DEM Site-based Alerts: Increased Site Selection Limit
The site selection limit for all DEM site-based alert configurations has increased from 10 to 100 sites.
DEM Alerts – Email Verification Failure
We have resolved an issue that previously hindered the successful completion of DEM alert email verification. Email verification for alert notifications is now functioning reliably, ensuring customers can confirm their email recipients without encountering errors.
DEM Tenant Overview “Client Versions In Use” Widget Update
The DEM Tenant Overview “Client Versions In Use” widget has been updated to use distinct device counts instead of session counts, so the numbers now better reflect the customer’s actual endpoint fleet.
DEM Enterprise API Availability (BETA)
We are launching the initial suite of Digital Experience Management (DEM) enterprise APIs in BETA to allow customers programmatic access to critical DEM data for integration into their proprietary workflows and tools. This release prioritizes the readiness and external availability of the most vital endpoints, enabling early adopters to commence integrating DEM metrics into their existing systems. These APIs are engineered to support enterprise-level environments, thereby assisting operations teams in monitoring digital experience with greater efficiency.
DEM Alerts – More Flexible User Experience Score Alert Conditions
DEM User Experience Score alerts now support additional configuration options for score, number of impacted users, and time duration, giving admins more precise control over when alerts are triggered. This added flexibility helps customers tune alerts to their environment so they can detect user experience issues earlier and reduce alert noise.

## Netskope One DSPM 12.1 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-12-1-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2026-03-17T20:18:56+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:30:26.771107+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 12.1 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 12.1 Release Notes
Major New Features
Refreshed data-at-rest dashboard report
We’ve refreshed the
Risk tab
within the DSPM Dashboard, providing a unified reporting hub that consolidates fragmented risk scores and scan results into a single, cohesive narrative. This update eliminates the need to manually piece together data protection stories by providing an end-to-end view of your security posture—from high-level infrastructure down to specific user identities and actions.
With these insights, security teams can:
Monitor risk posture from a high-level infrastructure view down to granular data classification and access details
Demonstrate security value to executive leadership with “at-a-glance” visibility into program effectiveness
Address SaaS data security risks using new widgets, such as Top Sensitive Data Exposed and Sensitive Files Exposed, to identify high-risk exposure points
Optimize organizational policies by centralizing insights across both SaaS and non-SaaS environments in one place
This enhancement reinforces Netskope’s leadership in data security by making complex data-at-rest insights accessible and actionable. The dashboard is automatically available to all DSPM users with reporting permissions across all management planes, no additional configuration required.
Improvements and Updates
Object-level policy updates
Netskope One DSPM now features object-level policy evaluations, moving beyond aggregate data store summaries to provide granular, per-file analysis for unstructured data. This enhancement allows the policy engine to return individual file matches and precise sensitive record counts, supported by new discovery signals such as service, region, and platform. Security teams can now monitor high-risk events with pinpoint precision across their entire data environment. To streamline automated response, these detailed object-level insights are consolidated within workflow payloads such as AWS SNS JSON, ensuring downstream security workflows receive the exact metadata needed for rapid remediation.
New option to use existing VPC when onboarding AWS EBS
AWS EBS volumes can now be onboarded and scanned using existing VPCs, subnets and security groups. This update eliminates the need for granting Netskope high-privileges to manage your VPCs & internet gateways, allowing organizations to maintain a policy of least privilege while scanning cloud block storage. To use this feature, simply specify your pre-configured AWS network information during the data store connection process.
Changes
Deprecation of emailed scheduled reporting
As part of our ongoing integration with Netskope Advanced Analytics (NAA), the standalone Scheduled Report functionality within DSPM is being deprecated to centralize reporting across the Netskope platform. Moving forward, users can leverage NAA for automated reporting needs, ensuring a consistent experience across all services. While automated scheduling within the DSPM module will be retired, administrators can still manually generate, download, and email reports directly to stakeholders as needed.

## Netskope One DSPM 12.2 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-12-2-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2026-06-24T20:49:35+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:30:37.848886+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 12.2 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 12.2 Release Notes
Major New Features
DSPM Privilege Analysis for SMB On-Premises File Shares
Netskope One DSPM now extends privilege analysis to on-premises SMB file shares, addressing a critical blind spot in modern data security. Due to decades of organic growth and the complexity of nested folder structures and Active Directory groups, security teams have historically been unable to determine who has access to what on SMB shares. This release closes that gap with deep visibility into effective access, risky permissions, and identity-based exposure.
With SMB Privilege Analysis, security teams can:
Detect sensitive files exposed org-wide via broad groups such as
Everyone
or
Domain Users
Identify ghost accounts — unresolved SIDs and disabled users — that retain access to sensitive files
Surface high-risk users holding excessive access to sensitive data
Detect broken inheritance at the folder level where a subfolder has been inadvertently opened up despite a secure parent tree
Resolve nested group membership up to 5 levels deep and folder hierarchies up to 20 levels, providing accurate effective access mapping
Privilege Analysis is enabled by default when onboarding a new SMB data store and requires an LDAP connection to map permissions to human identities. For existing SMB shares, users can enable the toggle via
Edit Data Store
settings. The feature contributes a new
Data Risk
score and
Stale User Risk Over-Privileged Data Store Risk
rating to the overall data store risk rating, reinforcing Netskope’s leadership in on-premises data security.
Improvements and Updates
Ability to select profiles used to fetch unstructured snippets
Users can now select which DLP Profiles should be used when fetching snippets for unstructured files. By giving users control over which specific DLP profiles are applied vs. using all profiles currently-enabled in the DSPM Discovery Profile, this reduces the time required to fetch snippets and allows for ad-hoc re-inspection of existing sensitive files.

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 135.0.0
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/virtual-appliance-release-notes-version-135-0-0/
**Last Modified:** 2026-03-31T15:22:53+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:30:42.324725+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 135.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 135.0.0
Release Date: March 31, 2026
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 135.0.0
Upgrading to version 135.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 128.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 128.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
450 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 110.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 135.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 128.0.0, 132.0.1 and 135.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 128.0.0
128.0.0
128.0.0
135.0.0
132.0.1
135.0.0
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.

## Netskope One DSPM 12.3 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-12-3-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2026-06-24T20:49:23+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:31:20.202599+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 12.3 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 12.3 Release Notes
Major New Features
Smart Scan for S3 and SMB
Large data stores present a fundamental challenge for data security: the sheer volume of files makes comprehensive scanning impractical, leaving security teams with incomplete visibility and risk assessments they can’t fully trust. Netskope One DSPM addresses this with
Smart Scan
— an intelligent discovery engine that finds more sensitive data, faster, without scanning every file.
Smart Scan uses adaptive, metadata-driven clustering to organize files into groups based on characteristics like file name, file type, folder structure, and size. It then concentrates scanning where sensitive data is actually located, going deeper into high-risk areas and lighter on areas that show no risk. The result is a scan that consistently identifies at least 90% of all Entity Data Types (EDTs) in a data store — while scanning a fraction of the total files.
With Smart Scan, security teams can:
Get a trustworthy risk picture across massive data stores
— covering billions of files without waiting days for results or sacrificing accuracy
See results as they happen
— findings appear in the UI progressively as the scan runs, so teams can begin investigating risk before a scan completes
Understand full exposure, not just what was scanned
— Smart Scan extrapolates a high-confidence estimate of total sensitive file count and data size across the entire data store, giving a complete view of risk magnitude
Rely on accuracy for small data stores
— data stores with 10,000 files or fewer are always scanned in full automatically
Smart Scan is the
default scanning mode
for all new DSPM scans. In this release, Smart Scan is available for
AWS S3 (IaaS)
and
SMB File Shares (On-Premises)
, with support for additional data store types planned in a future release.
Following the 12.3 release, customers utilizing a sidecar must upgrade to the latest sidecar version to enable these Smart Scan capabilities.
Smart Scan for SaaS
For SaaS applications, identifying which files pose real risk has always been a challenge — with thousands of files across Google Drive, SharePoint, OneDrive, Box, and Dropbox, not all files are equal in terms of risk. Netskope One DSPM now applies
Smart Scan to SaaS data stores
, ensuring the files surfaced in DSPM are always the ones that matter most.
Rather than surfacing an arbitrary selection of files, Smart Scan for SaaS prioritizes files that contain sensitive data — those that have triggered a DLP match for content such as PII, financial data, credentials, or other policy-matched data types. These files are guaranteed to appear in DSPM first, giving security teams immediate visibility into their highest-risk content across SaaS applications.
Improvements and Updates
Domain User Authentication for SQL Server
SQL Server data stores now support Domain User authentication, allowing organizations that manage SQL Server access via Active Directory to connect their data stores to DSPM without requiring SQL-native authentication credentials.
Microsoft Teams Webhook: Updated Format Support
DSPM webhook validation has been updated to support the new Microsoft Teams webhook format. Organizations using Teams for DSPM alert notifications will continue to receive alerts without requiring changes to their existing webhook configuration.
S3 Inventory Configuration Toggle
Users can now enable or disable the S3 Inventory configuration directly from the
Add/Edit Data Store
workflow for S3 buckets. This provides finer control over how DSPM collects file metadata for large S3 data stores, allowing teams to optimize scan performance based on their environment and bucket configuration.
“Preparing Metadata” Scan Stage
During Smart Scan, the Data Store Inventory page now displays a
“Preparing Metadata”
scan stage while the clustering algorithm is processing file metadata prior to sampling. This gives users clear visibility into scan progress and reduces confusion when a scan appears to be in a holding state before results begin appearing.

## Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for June 2026
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-digital-experience-management-release-notes-for-june-2026/
**Last Modified:** 2026-06-16T01:26:05+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:32:16.822261+00:00

Netskope Digital Experience Management Release Notes for June 2026
The following is a list of Digital Experience Management (DEM) releases for the month of June 2026:
Aggregated Traceroute
Aggregated Traceroute gives administrators a unified view of the network path between a user’s device and the Netskope cloud across time. Unlike a traditional traceroute that captures a single instant, this feature aggregates probe data over a selected time window so you can see how the path and its latency evolved, identify which hops are consistently problematic, and correlate network issues with user location.
The feature introduces three interconnected views that work together to streamline network troubleshooting:
End-to-End Underlay Latency — time-series chart of round-trip time from client to POP
Hop-by-Hop Path View — aggregated network graph showing every hop, link latency, and probe distribution
Time Slider with Location Awareness — a contextual filter that ties network behavior to where the user was
To learn more, see
User Overview — Metrics
.
DEM User Details: Zoom In on Collapsed Sections
Previously, using the zoom in feature on the User Details page did not expand collapsed sections, leaving content invisible. This has been resolved and the zoom in feature now correctly expands and renders all sections regardless of their collapsed state.

## Netskope One DSPM 12.4 Release Notes
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/netskope-one-dspm-12-4-release-notes/
**Last Modified:** 2026-06-24T20:51:59+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:32:27.197183+00:00

Netskope One DSPM 12.4 Release Notes - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Netskope One DSPM 12.4 Release Notes
Ensure that your sidecars are at least version 12.3 in order to take full advantage of the latest Netskope One DSPM features, including Smart Scan.
Major New Features
Single Appliance deployment model
Netskope One DSPM now supports a Single Appliance deployment model that combines the DLP appliance and DSPM sidecar into a single, unified instance. This significantly improves on-premises infrastructure deployment by eliminating the need to manage separate components for DLP processing and DSPM scanning.
With the Single Appliance deployment model, organizations can:
Simplify initial setup.
Deploy one appliance instead of managing separate DLP and sidecar instances, reducing deployment time, configuration complexity, and infrastructure maintenance.
Download the appliance image directly from the DSPM tenant
. Users no longer need to visit a separate download portal and navigate a confusing series of buttons that have nothing to do with DSPM. Now you click just one button to access the image!
Manage both the appliance and sidecars from a unified UI.
View and configure both from the Sidecar Administration page that exists in DSPM today, which has been enhanced to show greater detail and telemetry.
Control your appliance upgrades straight from DSPM.
See your appliance upgrade schedule, configure it to match your organization’s needs, or manually kick it off at your leisure. Monitor the history of your appliance and sidecar upgrade history using the new detail view.
Improvements and Updates
Snowflake scan duration capping
Snowflake scans now support capping the duration of sampling queries, preventing long-running full table scans on large fields. This prevents Snowflake from racking up unnecessary usage bills while still providing for DSPM’s clarification capabilities & risk assessments.
Abort Queued Scans
Users can now abort scans that are in a queued state before they begin execution. Previously, only active scans could be cancelled.
Improved on-screen display when DB Role Count is not available
When DB Role Count analysis is unavailable for a data store, the UI now displays a clear restriction message explaining why the analysis cannot be performed, rather than showing an empty or confusing state. This addresses an issue where the current icon and tooltip may appear misleading or alarming due to the limited context provided (for example with S3, an object storage service which does not have the concept of database roles).
